request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to the sheet is now written to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What was missing:** the server didn't know who was signed in. The name only lived in the browser's URL.

**Front end**
- `api/http.ts`: `postJson` and `putJson` can now take the user and send it in an `X-User` header.
- `PersonForm.tsx` and `ClaimForm.tsx` pass the signed-in user when they save.

**Server**
- Each of the four write endpoints has a new `audit` step, which runs after the change is applied and before the response. The new classes are `AuditPersonAdded`, `AuditPersonEdited`, `AuditClaimAdded` and `AuditClaimEdited`.
- A refused change (bad amount, duplicate name, unknown person or claim, or any later rule that fails earlier in the pipeline) stops before the audit step, so it writes no line.
- Amounts use the same two-decimal formatting the screen shows, and dates are yyyy-mm-dd.
- `CLAIM_EDITED` looks up the claim's person to get their name.
- `Audit.java` gained two helpers: `line(...)` builds a record (event, `sheet=`, `by=`, then the fields, single-spaced) and `user(...)` reads the `X-User` header.

**Things to know:**
- **Header reading:** my first try used Spring's `@RequestHeader`, but OfficeFloor ignores it and `by=` came out empty. The steps now read the header through OfficeFloor's `ServerHttpConnection`.
- **Rollback:** the audit line is written inside the save, just before it is committed. If the database failed at that last moment, the line would already be written even though the change was rolled back.
- **The user isn't checked:** the server takes the name as given. A request without the header is recorded as `by=` with nothing after it. That matches how sign-in already works (you just type a name, with no password).
